extracted.intended_audience: delegates and policymakers at the United Nations food conference; international policy makers and informed public interested in post-war food policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and concrete proposals for international food and agricultural policy to secure adequate nutrition after the war, including buffer stocks, international organizations, trade rules, and short- and long-term production policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: secure, adequate, suitable food supply for all
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference should go on record that the common goal is "to insure to all mankind a supply of food which is secure, adequate and suitable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pledge to make the better nutrition of all peoples a primary objective of policy; the declaration should state this goal as the guiding principle of international action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider both phases of post-war shortage
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference should consider both phases of the period of shortage: (1) the immediate phase dominated by relieving hunger (energy foods) and (2) a transition phase when enough food exists to relieve hunger but not enough for a balanced diet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must address urgent relief needs and also policies for transition to balanced diets; do not confine discussion only to wartime production or relief organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: International arrangements to encourage maximum production and equitable distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve that international arrangements should exist "to encourage the maximum production of the commodities which are most needed and to secure an orderly and equitable distribution of the commodities which are in short supply."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such arrangements may include coordinated purchase, allocation and transportation machinery, and should assist relief organizers to find supplies when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a bold policy of expansion rather than restricted production
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend a bold policy of expansion in place of restriction; the only unquestionable justification for reducing production is to release capacity for producing some other more desirable commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct effort toward stimulating consumption and increasing production rather than restricting output as was done in inter-war periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an internationally held buffer stock / food bank
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose an internationally held balancing or buffer stock (food bank) that can be increased when production outruns demand and drawn upon when it falls short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a stock has a double purpose: insure consumers ample supplies and producers a purchaser, while shielding both from violent short-term price fluctuations; it should combine short-period price stabilization with a long-period price policy to favor efficient producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buffer stock price management
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority operating the buffer stock should vary the prices at which it buys and sells so as to stabilize prices short-term and allow steady expansion to efficient producers long-term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use variations in buy/sell price points to achieve combined short-term stabilization and long-term development goals; this model differs from a stock designed simply to maintain prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: No regulation by quotas except under representative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference should declare that 'there should be no regulation by quotas of the export of any agricultural commodity except under the control of some authority fully representative of both producers and consumers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation by quotas should only occur under representative authorities; prefer buffer-stock management over export/production quotas as the primary tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorities should coordinate under an international co-ordinating body
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities responsible for regulation of various commodities should keep close contact and be subject to the policy direction of a representative international co-ordinating body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinating body should direct desirable shifts in production and ensure commodity authorities' policies are harmonized for global benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create international body to buy and distribute food to needy populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend creation of an internationally financed organization empowered to buy foodstuffs and give them to populations in need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism would be the appropriate way to deal with cases where free distribution is required; it should avoid creating permanent dependence and should be one tool among others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid destruction of surplus foodstuffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid destruction of foodstuffs in 'surplus' supply and discuss measures to ensure such destruction can be avoided in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surpluses should be managed via buffer stocks, redistribution, or international purchase/distribution mechanisms rather than destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a new comprehensive organization for food and agriculture
rubrics_metrics.description: A new and comprehensive organization should be created to study problems continuously, collect scientific and statistical data, and provide expert advice and assistance to governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions include maintaining reliable statistics, initiating studies, issuing reports, advising on free distribution, providing experts to governments, and promoting experimental international research on agriculture and nutrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term priority: energy foods to relieve hunger
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first phase of post-war shortages the dominant problem is relieving hunger; the main task is to provide enough energy foods, as these are what relieves hunger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize energy foods initially; do not prematurely switch production from energy foods to protective foods needed later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature switch from energy to protective foods
rubrics_metrics.description: Warn against the mistake of switching production from energy foods to protective foods too early during shortage phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan production sequencing so that immediate hunger is relieved first, then transition to protective/nutrient-rich foods as supply permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve consumption habits through education and persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving diets is achievable by guiding people in the use of what is available; education and persuasion are essential components of any better food program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to give people what they like eating while leading them to like more nutritious foods; use public guidance, schooling, and community programs to effect change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidize production and consumption of protective foods and provide communal meals
rubrics_metrics.description: Production and consumption of protective foods (e.g., milk) should be subsidized; communal meals for school children and factory workers and price adjustments can encourage nutritious consumption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subsidies and public provisioning to improve access to protective foods in industrialized countries where consumers buy most food.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply minimum quality and nutritive standards to staple foods (fortification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve diets by applying minimum standards of quality and nutritive value to staple foods, for example by adding vitamins to margarine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement fortification and quality standards even under shortage conditions to improve population nutrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate basic principles of agricultural production
rubrics_metrics.description: Enunciate basic principles of food production such as maintenance of soil fertility, prevention of erosion, distribution of fertilizers, and promotion of balanced agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles should form general guidance adaptable country-by-country, helping to place food production and consumption on an enduring and progressive basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage shifts to more desirable commodities and efficient producers
rubrics_metrics.description: One object of regulation should be to encourage desirable shifts in production from one commodity to another and from less to more efficient producers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy instruments (buffer stocks, price policy, coordinating bodies) should incentivize reallocation of capacity toward higher-priority or more efficient outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize link between food policy and wider economic policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Food and agricultural policy are closely interrelated with international economic policy—monetary arrangements, commercial policy, and international investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference consideration of food problems should include reference to wider economic problems since these influence and are influenced by food policy outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address instability caused by unpredictable agricultural surpluses
rubrics_metrics.description: Because exact quantities produced cannot be accurately determined in advance, international markets experienced disorder from periodic 'surpluses' leading to price collapse and production restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use buffer stocks and coordinated international policy to avoid boom-and-slump cycles that harm both producers and consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop machinery for coordinated purchase, allocation and transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate an international production program and maintain machinery for coordinated purchase, allocation and transportation of commodities to ensure best use of supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such machinery will help avoid post-war repetition of chaotic market outcomes and facilitate efficient distribution to areas in need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and maintain comparable, up-to-date agricultural and nutrition statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The international organization should keep a reliable body of statistics and other information, collected on comparable bases and kept up-to-date by experts, covering main agricultural commodities and nutrition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliable data should underpin study, planning, exchange of information, and advice to governments; statistics should extend to nutrition and related economic/social factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use international organization to assist experimental research
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization might initiate international collaboration in experimental research on agriculture and nutrition whose development would benefit all nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for shared experimental research can accelerate improvements in production methods and nutrition that are globally beneficial.
